speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; these are significant symptoms that require a careful evaluation. To begin, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits, such as diarrhea, constipation, or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The abdominal pain and weight loss are concerning; have you noticed any blood in your stool or black, tarry stools recently? Additionally, have you experienced any difficulty swallowing or food getting stuck in your throat?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma

The combination of painless, fixed supraclavicular lymphadenopathy with B-symptoms (night sweats, weight loss) and abdominal pain is highly suspicious for an underlying malignancy, particularly Hodgkin Lymphoma. I need to confirm this with imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: CT Chest, Abdomen, and Pelvis.
